land.text: the Grand Duchy of Baden, whose Grand Duke fled Karlsruhe on the night of 13/14 May 1849

predecessors.note: The Grand Duchy dossier of this project records the loss to counterpart republic-of-baden in May 1849.

land.text: the grand duchy, restored when Rastatt surrendered on 23 July 1849

successors.note: Cliopatria draws the Republic of Baden shape to 1852 and has no Grand Duchy shape in 1849-1852; the Grand Duchy dossier corrects that.

capitals.name: Karlsruhe
capitals.note: The page names no seat for the provisional government; it says only that the Grand Duke fled 'from his residenz in Karlsruhe' and that the government retreated to Freiburg in late June, with Rastatt 'the last bastion of the revolutionaries'. Karlsruhe is a reading.

correction.text: The Grand Duchy of Baden as in Cliopatria's 1848 shape, held by the revolutionaries from the night of 13/14 May to 23 July 1849 and only in 1849 (Cliopatria runs the row to 1852)

keyframe_review.note: 17,733 km2 = 73 grid cells: 57 of the 59 cells of the Grand Duchy's 1848 shape plus 16 cells in the Bavarian Rhenish Palatinate (49.1-49.6 N, 7.4-8.2 E; Rhineland-Palatinate), which the page does not place under Baden's provisional government (it mentions the Palatinate only as a second centre of the revolution, whose troops the Prussians ousted by 20 June 1849). Area check: the later Republic of Baden page gives Baden 15,070 km2 in 1925, so Cliopatria's figure is 1.18 times it; 14,176 km2 for the grand duchy shape is 0.94 times it. The years are the larger error: the page ends the rebellion on 23 July 1849, Cliopatria draws the row to 1852.

region.text: Karlsruhe and Rastatt: the garrison at Rastatt mutinied on 9 May and the Grand Duke fled Karlsruhe

ledger.note: 13/14 May 1849: the Rastatt garrison has mutinied (9 May) and Grand Duke Leopold flees Karlsruhe, so Baden passes to the revolutionaries. 'That same night of 13/14 May Grand Duke Leopold flees from his residenz in Karlsruhe into exile at Koblenz.'

region.text: the grand duchy, held by the revolutionaries; the page names no limit to their hold

ledger.note: May 1849: the revolutionaries take the grand duchy; on 1 June 'Under Lorenz Brentano a provisional democratic government is formed'. The page says the Baden Constituent Assembly 'only lasted from 10 June to 30 June 1849' and that Amand Goegg's question 'about the proclamation of the republic' found no support on 12/13 May: it names no proclaimed republic. The whole grand duchy is the reading (Freiburg was rebel-held, Rastatt 'the last bastion').

region.text: the grand duchy, invaded by Prussian, federal and Hessian troops

ledger.note: June 1849: Prussian, federal and Hessian troops invade Baden 'in order to defeat the revolution'; Hirschfeld wins at Waghausel on 21/22 June and a dictatorial government under Goegg and Werner forms on 28 June. The grand duke's side is carried by Prussia and the Confederation's troops; the Grand Duchy ledger names this row as its counterpart.

23 July 1849: Rastatt surrenders. 'After being surrounded for three weeks Rastaat surrenders to Groeben'; on 7 July 'The Prussians march into Freiburg unopposed' and on 12 July revolutionary troops cross into Switzerland and ask for asylum.

region.text: the grand duchy, restored to its grand duke

ledger.note: 23 July 1849: the revolutionaries lose Baden. 'The rebellion ended on 23 July 1849 with the military defeat of the last revolt and the capture of Rastatt Fortress'; the Baden Army was disbanded and later rebuilt under Prussian leadership.
23 July 1849: the revolutionary government ends with the fall of Rastatt; the grand duchy passes back to its grand duke.

wars.name: Baden Revolution

zones.text: the grand duchy, invaded in June 1849 and cleared by 23 July

wars.outcome: The Prussian-led invasion beat the revolutionaries at Waghausel (21/22 June), entered Freiburg (7 July) and took Rastatt (23 July 1849), ending the revolution.
wars.note: The page does not say how long Prussian troops stayed in Baden; the Grand Duchy dossier bridges the end of the occupation to 1852.

certainty.note: The revolutionaries held the grand duchy within its existing frontiers; no page opened states those frontiers' survey, so this is an inherited-frontier reading. The front lines of June-July 1849 moved but are not drawn.

sources.title: Baden Revolution
sources.note: Dated narrative: 9 May mutiny, 13/14 May flight, 1 June provisional government, June invasion, Waghausel, 7 July Freiburg, 23 July Rastatt, 12 July refuge in Switzerland.

sources.title: Republic of Baden
sources.note: The WRONG state: the article is the Republic of Baden of 1918-1945 (Cliopatria's Wikipedia field points to it). Used only for Baden's 1925 area (15,070 km2) and to document the mismatch.

notes: WRONG LINKS. Cliopatria's Wikipedia field 'Republic of Baden' and Wikidata Q690821 are the title and id of the 1918-1945 Weimar-era state, whose page the second source shows; the 1849 row is the revolutionary government of the Baden Revolution, so the dossier links 'Baden Revolution' and leaves wikidata null. The Baden Revolution page does not say a republic was proclaimed in 1849 (it records a provisional democratic government formed on 1 June under Lorenz Brentano and an unsupported 12/13 May question about proclaiming the republic). SHAPE: Cliopatria's 17,733 km2 shape is the grand duchy plus 16 cells of the Bavarian Rhenish Palatinate; the page connects the Palatinate only as a second centre of the revolution, so the correction uses the grand duchy alone. The Palatinate's own revolutionary government (May-June 1849, troops ousted by the First Prussian Corps by 20 June) needs a dossier from the group that owns it (suggested slug provisional-government-of-the-palatinate); this batch did not open a page on it. YEARS: Cliopatria draws 1849-1852 and has no Grand Duchy shape in those years; the grand-duchy-of-baden dossier already restores the grand duchy for 1849-1852. SILENCES: the page gives no area, no fixed seat for the provisional government, and no limit to the land the rebels held beyond Freiburg and Rastatt.
